correctness.rationale: Every noise Kraus operator is an independent-coordinate Pauli flip; the t-fold convolution is the classical hypercube coordinate-flip law. Hadamard conjugation makes a generalized dephasing channel. Explicit measure-and-prepare degradation and Pauli twirling plus established coherent-information concavity yield capacity as dimension minus Shannon entropy. Fixed parity yields the one-qubit floor and the exact relative-entropy identity. Pairing complementary Fourier characters yields an orthogonal expansion of the likelihood ratio on the parity class; a Gaussian-Hermite limit and a uniform exponential-series L2 tail bound imply lognormal convergence with uniformly integrable L log L, giving the claimed constant the exponential critical-window coefficient. Data processing and strict monotonicity of the limit give the crossing time. Exact integer enumeration, Kraus Choi spectra, and high-dimensional radial recurrence computations pass 136 finite checks, not treated as infinite proof.
risks: The asymptotic error is not claimed uniform in growing scaled time.
Finite numerical samples do not establish an infinite limit.

originality.rationale: The originality judgment is confined to the sharp parity-periodic relative-entropy/quantum-capacity critical profile and its fixed-excess first-crossing law. Quillen derives the underlying averaged walk; Devetak–Shor establishes the general one-letter dephasing capacity principle; Diaconis–Graham–Morrison establishes a total-variation profile for a similar but lazy classical chain. Neither general dephasing capacity nor a total-variation profile logically specifies this nonlazy parity-conditioned KL limit with uniform-integrability control. Searches of published mathematical records did not identify this combined sharp statement; the 1990 full-text access gap is explicitly recorded, and priority remains provisional.

value.rationale: The exact model-specific capacity window answers a motivated information-retention question left qualitative in Quillen 2026: how long Haar-coin averaging takes to reduce transmissible quantum information to the parity-protected qubit. It identifies a nontrivial universal critical coefficient and the first time at which any fixed excess rate vanishes, rather than a small finite lookup. Deriving the KL coefficient demands a parity-class Fourier expansion, Hermite limit, and control of logarithmic moments; known variation distance results are insufficient as stated. The result can benchmark a concrete noisy quantum walk but makes no generic quantum-error-correction or arbitrary-graph claim.
risks: Operational usefulness is model-specific and concerns averaged independent channel uses; extension to particular coin realizations is not proved.
